subtitle: How Bajirao Turned Thirst into a Weapon at Palkhed

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a lone rider on a dark horizon, cavalry massed as shadows behind
panels.action: Peshwa Bajirao I sits tall on horseback at dusk on the Deccan plain, cloak whipping in the wind, with distant dust clouds hinting at fast-moving Maratha horse behind him.

dialogue.text: Peshwa Bajirao I, in the troubled Deccan of 1727–1728, faces the Nizam’s guns with only speed, thirst, and patience as his chosen weapons.

i18n.hi: सन् १७२७–२८ के अशांत दक्कन में पेशवा बाजीराव प्रथम निज़ाम की तोपों के सामने सिर्फ़ रफ़्तार, प्यास और सब्र से उतरते हैं।

panels.shot: broad bird’s-eye over the Deccan plateau showing rivers, forts, and marching armies marked by dust plumes
panels.action: A vast view of the Deccan plateau stretches under a harsh sun, rivers winding through dry fields, distant fort-topped hills watching two opposing clouds of army dust creeping toward each other.

dialogue.text: By the late 1720s the Deccan was a board of rival claims: Mughal farmans, Maratha chauth, old sultanate rights, and the new power of Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah.

i18n.hi: १७२० के आख़िरी सालों तक दक्कन दावों का अखाड़ा था – मुग़ल फ़रमान, मराठा चौथ, पुराने सुल्तानों के हक़ और नई ताक़त निज़ाम‑उल‑मुल्क आसफ़ जાહ की।

panels.shot: interior court wide shot of Shaniwar-style wada hall in Pune, low-angle on empty seat of the Peshwa
panels.action: Inside a Pune wada hall, mats, ledgers and spears lean against polished pillars, while a low platform with cushions stands empty, hinting at a recent council of war.

dialogue.text: In Pune, the young Peshwa Bajirao had already stumbled in early campaigns. Critics whispered that his daring outpaced his caution.

i18n.hi: पुणे में जवान पेशवा बाजीराव शुरुआती मुहिमों में डगमगा चुके थे। लोग फुसफुसाते, उसकी हिम्मत उसकी सतर्कता से आगे भागती है।

panels.shot: medium close-up across a wooden table map, candlelight on Bajirao’s intense face
panels.action: Peshwa Bajirao I leans over a rough cloth map spread on a wooden table, fingers tracing rivers and ghats, his brows knit in concentration as a dim oil lamp throws hard shadows.

dialogue.text: He studied the land instead of his pride: rivers, wells, harvest cycles, the time a bullock cart took to climb a ghat.

i18n.hi: उसने अहम अपने अहं से नहीं, ज़मीन से सीखा – नदियाँ, कुएँ, फ़सल का समय, बैलगाड़ी को घाट चढ़ने में लगने वाला वक़्त।

panels.shot: interior of the Nizam’s camp tent, low-angle on a richly dressed silhouette against flapping canvas
panels.action: Inside a grand tent with embroidered walls, a regal silhouette in Mughal robes points toward a map while officers stand in attendance, spears and matchlocks stacked near the entrance.

dialogue.text: To the east, Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah gathered a heavy army—artillery, slow baggage, and noble retainers—to check Maratha claims in Berar and Khandesh.

i18n.hi: पूरब में निज़ाम‑उल‑मुल्क आसफ़ जাহ ने भारी लश्कर जमा किया – तोपख़ाना, सुस्त सामान ढोने वाले, और खानदानी सवार – ताकि बेरार और खांदेश में मराठा दावों को रोके।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of cavalry streaming out of Pune gate, tracking shot alongside Bajirao
panels.action: Peshwa Bajirao I rides at the head of a long column of light Maratha cavalry pouring out of a city gate, horse hooves kicking up dry dust as the walls of Pune recede behind them.

dialogue.text: In 1727, as the Nizam advanced, Bajirao chose not to guard one fort but to unleash the one thing he had and the Nizam lacked—speed.

i18n.hi: १७२७ में निज़ाम बढ़ा तो बाजीराव ने किसी एक क़िले की रखवाली नहीं, अपने पास की एक चीज़ छोड़ दी – रफ़्तार, जो निज़ाम के पास नहीं थी।

panels.shot: wide shot over Berar countryside, low-angle of riders passing burning grain stacks in distance
panels.action: Bajirao rides across an open Berar landscape while far behind him, smoke rises from fields and storehouses, villagers driving cattle away from the line of the Nizam’s advance.

dialogue.text: He struck Berar, Mahur, Washim—zones rich in revenue. Not for glory alone, but to cut the Nizam’s income and unsettle his rear.

i18n.hi: उसने बेरार, माहूर, वाशीम जैसे धन वाले इलाक़ों पर धावा बोला – शौक़ के लिए नहीं, निज़ाम की आमदनी काटने और उसके पीछे का इलाका हिलाने के लिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Burhanpur’s walls from outside, with distant horsemen on a ridge
panels.action: The walls and domes of Burhanpur rise over the Tapti river, guarded and alert, as on a distant ridge a small knot of Maratha horsemen watch, silhouetted against the sky.

dialogue.text: He threatened Burhanpur, Mughal key to the north-south artery, to show that the Maratha spear could reach deep while the Nizam lumbered after him.

i18n.hi: उसने बुर्हानपुर, उत्तर–दक्षिण की मुग़ल नस पर ख़तरा तान दिया, दिखा दिया कि मराठा भाला दूर तक चुभ सकता है जबकि निज़ाम पीछे लड़खड़ाता रहे।

panels.shot: close-up on Bajirao in council with a village headman at night by firelight
panels.action: Seated cross-legged under a tree at night, Bajirao listens intently to a turbaned village headman, a small fire burning between them, horses resting in the shadows.

dialogue.text: Letters from the Peshwa’s daftar show a campaign of persuasion and pressure: village heads warned, supplies diverted, revenue chests moved ahead of the Nizam’s path.

i18n.hi: पेशवे के दफ़्तर से मिलती चिट्ठियाँ बताती हैं – समझाने और दबाव की मुहिम, गाँवों के मुखिया चेताए गए, रसद मोड़ी गई, और मालख़ाने निज़ाम की राह से पहले ही खिसका दिए गए।

panels.shot: long shot of Nizam’s massive column winding slowly through rough terrain, viewed from a hilltop
panels.action: A long, slow snake of ox-drawn guns, covered carts, and infantry creeps along a rough road, officers on elephants urging them on under a high unforgiving sun.

dialogue.text: The Nizam followed with dignity but with weight. His artillery and courtly train demanded fodder, grain, and water that Bajirao had already emptied.

i18n.hi: निज़ाम शान से चला, पर बोझ लेकर। उसका तोपख़ाना और दरबारी क़ाफ़िला चारे, अनाज और पानी के लिए तरसता, जिन्हें बाजीराव पहले ही साफ़ कर चुके थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bajirao on horseback, gesturing cavalry away from a distant enemy army
panels.action: On a dusty plain, Bajirao reins his horse sharply, one arm outstretched ordering his riders to wheel away even as a distant line of Nizamite standards glimmer on the far horizon.

dialogue.text: “We do not feed his guns with our dead. We feed his march with hunger.”

i18n.hi: "हम उसकी तोपों को अपने लाशों से नहीं भरते, उसकी चाल को भूख से भरते हैं।"

panels.shot: close-up of Nizam’s officers in a heated debate inside a field tent
panels.action: Inside a crowded field tent, Nizam’s commanders argue over a worn map, one jabbing a finger in frustration while another looks exhausted, sweat darkening their turbans.

dialogue.text: In the Nizam’s camp, confusion grew. Reports of raided districts, vanished revenue, and empty granaries arrived faster than his troops could march.

i18n.hi: निज़ाम के डेरे में घबराहट बढ़ी – लुटे परगनों, ग़ायब महसूल, खाली कोठारों की ख़बरें उसके सिपाहियों से तेज़ चलती रहीं।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot of Palkhed region, highlighting rivers and dry channels under sun
panels.action: From above, the landscape around Palkhed shows a river threading through rocky ground, sparse trees clinging to its banks, while large stretches of dry, cracked earth stretch away.

dialogue.text: Bajirao chose his snare near Palkhed, where rivers and streams could be turned into chains if an army depended on them.

i18n.hi: बाजीराव ने जाल पलखेड के पास चुना, जहाँ नदियाँ–नाले वही ज़ंजीर बन सकते थे, अगर कोई फ़ौज उन पर ही टिकी हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bajirao on a ridge overlooking Nizam’s camp near the river, dawn light
panels.action: At dawn, Bajirao sits motionless on his horse atop a ridge, watching the Nizam’s sprawling camp clustered tightly near a river, campfires smoking weakly in the chill air.

dialogue.text: He let the Nizam cross and settle, heavy camp close to the water. Then he closed the circle—fast horse on every approach and ford.

i18n.hi: उसने निज़ाम को नाला पार करने और पानी किनारे भारी डेरे डालने दिया, फिर घेरा कस दिया – हर रास्ते, हर घाट पर तेज़ घोड़े सवार।

panels.shot: ground-level shot from inside Nizam’s camp, exhausted soldiers eyeing a shrinking waterline
panels.action: Within the Nizam’s camp, weary soldiers crowd around the riverbank, their faces drawn, as the waterline lies farther down the bank, carts and animals straining in the heat.

dialogue.text: No grand clash announced their danger. It came slowly, as fodder vanished, grain wagons failed to arrive, and even the river could not serve so many for long.

i18n.hi: कोई बड़ी टकराहट ने खतरे का ऐलान नहीं किया – ख़तरा चुपचाप आया, जब चारा ग़ायब हुआ, अनाज की गाड़ियाँ रुक गईं, और नदी भी इतने लोगों को ज़्यादा दिन न संभाल सकी।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of Maratha horse arching around the Nizam’s encampment, seen from above and behind Bajirao
panels.action: From behind Bajirao’s shoulder, lines of Maratha horsemen can be seen fanning out around the distant Nizam encampment, small fast-moving knots cutting off roads and tracks like tightening cords.

dialogue.text: Maratha bands did not storm the camp; they sealed it. Every path that might bring grain or release was shadowed by riders who appeared and vanished with the dust.

i18n.hi: मराठा दलों ने डेरे पर धावा नहीं बोला, उसे मुहरबंद कर दिया – हर राह जो अनाज या राहत ला सकती थी, धूल में आते–जाते सवारों की परछाइयों में खो गई।

panels.shot: close-up of a Nizamite messenger on a tired horse, blocked by calm Maratha riders at a ford
panels.action: At a shallow river crossing, a lone Nizamite messenger on a lathered horse pulls up short as a small group of Maratha horsemen watches him silently from the opposite bank, hands resting lightly on spears.

dialogue.text: Messages for help met silent riders at fords and ferries. The great Mughal-trained general found himself trapped not by walls but by emptiness.

i18n.hi: मदद की पुकारें जब घाटों और नावों तक पहुँचीं, तो सामने मौन सवार थे – मुग़ल के इस बड़े उस्ताद सेनानी को दीवारों ने नहीं, खालीपन ने क़ैद कर लिया।

panels.shot: interior of the Nizam’s tent, subdued, with the Nizam seated in thought, a letter in hand
panels.action: Inside a quieter tent, the Nizam sits heavily on a low seat, a letter drooping from his hand, while a single lamp burns and an aide waits anxiously by the entrance.

dialogue.text: Asaf Jah was no fool; he read the land as well. He knew that each passing day fed Bajirao’s strength and his own army’s weakness.

i18n.hi: आसफ़ जाह भी नादान न था; वह भी ज़मीन पढ़ता था। उसे समझ आया हर गुज़रता दिन बाजीराव को मज़बूत और उसकी अपनी फ़ौज को कमज़ोर कर रहा है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bajirao receiving emissaries in an open field camp, both sides standing
panels.action: In an open field camp with only simple tents, Bajirao stands bareheaded, meeting richly dressed envoys who bow slightly, his officers and standard-bearers forming a quiet semicircle behind him.

dialogue.text: So emissaries rode between the camps. The path to peace now ran through Bajirao’s tents, not the Nizam’s cannons.

i18n.hi: तो सुलह के सवार दोनों डेरे के बीच दौड़े। अब अमन का रास्ता निज़ाम की तोपों से नहीं, बाजीराव के तंबुओं से होकर जाता था।

panels.shot: close-up on hands exchanging a rolled document sealed with cords, neutral background
panels.action: Two pairs of hands meet in the center of the frame, one in Maratha cuffs, the other in Mughal-style sleeves, as a rolled document tied with cords passes from one to the other.

dialogue.text: On 6 March 1728, at Mungi-Shevgaon, a treaty sealed the Nizam’s acceptance of Maratha claims—an agreement born from empty fields and guarded wells.

i18n.hi: ६ मार्च १७२८ को मुंगी–शेवगांव में एक संधि ने मराठा दावों को निज़ाम से मनवा लिया – ये समझौता खाली खेतों और पहरेदार कुओं की कोख से पैदा हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bajirao in a quiet moment after the treaty, seated, looking at a map thoughtfully
panels.action: Later, Bajirao sits alone in a modest tent, map unrolled before him, fingers resting near Palkhed, his face thoughtful rather than triumphant as wind stirs the canvas flap.

dialogue.text: For Bajirao, Palkhed was not a legend of invincibility but a lesson: that power lay as much in grain ledgers and water rights as in steel.

i18n.hi: बाजीराव के लिए पलखेड कोई अजेयता की कहानी नहीं, सबक़ था – ताक़त उतनी ही अनाज की किताबों और पानी के हक़ में थी, जितनी फ़ौलाद में।

panels.shot: wide closing shot of the Deccan landscape at sunset, roads and rivers glowing, faint silhouettes of riders
panels.action: The Deccan plain stretches under a red sunset, rivers catching the last light, faint silhouettes of horsemen moving like small shadows across the vast land.

dialogue.text: The campaign of Palkhed showed India a new kind of war: victory without pitched battle, where the sharpest blade was the mind that reached the river first.

i18n.hi: पलखेड की मुहिम ने हिंदुस्तान को जंग की नई सूरत दिखाई – बिना बड़ी भिड़ंत के फ़तह, जहाँ सबसे तेज़ धार उस दिमाग़ की थी जो पहले नदी तक पहुँचा।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Bajirao Turned Thirst into a Weapon at Palkhed
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे बाजीराव ने प्यास को पलखेड में हथियार बनाया
